utility.notes: The City of Gridley operates its own municipal electric utility, confirmed via the city's own Electric Department page. This is a municipal utility, not PG&E, independently confirmed rather than assumed from county location — the rest of Butte County researched this session (Chico, Oroville, Paradise) is PG&E territory.

value.name: Gridley Electric Utility
value.notes: Gridley Electric Utility is a municipal utility; Pioneer Community Energy's own homepage (directly re-verified this session) describes its current service area as Placer/El Dorado county communities only and does not include any Butte County city. As a municipal utility, Gridley does not participate in a CCA the way IOU-served cities do — the city's own municipal utility is both the distribution and generation provider.

permit_authority.value: Gridley Electric Utility (interconnection), then Butte County Department of Development Services Building Division (permit)
permit_authority.notes: Gridley's own Building Inspection Services are performed by Butte County's Development Services Building Division, per the city's own site.

interconnection_url.notes: As a municipal utility, Gridley's own Electric Department interconnection process (Solar 2.0 Program) applies rather than a statewide IOU NEM program.

value.name: Application for Solar Installations in Gridley

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own Electric Department FAQ, 'How to Enroll in the Gridley Solar 2.0 Program?'; all new systems and existing NEM systems expanding more than 10% must complete the Interconnection Agreement and obtain the proper permits.

value: Gridley's building inspections are performed by the Butte County Department of Development Services Building Division
Schedule an inspection through the Butte County Accela Public Portal; a user account linked to the permit is required
Contact the Building Division at 530-552-3699 / dsbuilding@buttecounty.net for assistance with the Public Portal
inspection_steps.notes: This is Butte County's general Building Division inspection process (covers all permit types, including solar), since Gridley's own building inspections are performed by the County; the City does not publish a separate, solar-specific inspection sequence.

value.program_or_pathway: Solar 2.0 Program (customer-generator interconnection applied for on or after January 22, 2020)
other_conditions: System must be solar, wind, or a hybrid electric system located behind the meter at the customer's premises
Designed to offset up to 100% of the customer's annual kWh load, capped at 1,000kW
A multi-register meter is installed at the customer's expense to separately track consumption and surplus generation
Surplus generation is credited at a buyback rate of $0.045/kWh; customers who applied before January 22, 2020 remain on standard Net Energy Metering unless they choose to switch

value.name: Application Review Fee - Photovoltaic/Solar Electric Generating Facility Rated at 10 kW or Less
Application Review Fee - Photovoltaic/Solar Electric Generating Facility Rated Higher than 10 kW

permit_fees.notes: Per the City's own Electric Department FAQ: 'The following Application Review Fees are due at the time of application submittals.' Customers installing solar are also assessed the cost of a multi-register meter upgrade/installation if one is not already present, per a separate FAQ answer, but no dollar amount was stated for that item.
